introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0585 RELIGIOUS STUDIES 1, JUNE 2017, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Section heading: Personal and Social Relationships and Problems, answer all 50 questions. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use an HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed "0585 Religious Studies 1 - Ordinary Level". Answer ALL questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully and then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Indecent dressing gives the impression of someone who

*Options as printed:* A) Wants to attract People.   B) Is immoral and is a seducer.   C) Very ugly.   D) Very beautiful or handsome.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Christian moral teaching, indecent dressing is read by others as a sign of immodesty or a wish to seduce. Ugliness and beauty have nothing to do with the way a person dresses, and "wants to attract people" is too weak to name the moral impression created. Options A and B are both defensible, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Is immoral and is a seducer).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: A person who sees nothing wrong in using another person's property without his or her permission has
questions.corrige_markdown:
A lax conscience is one that is too easy-going: it excuses wrong acts such as taking another person's property without asking. An erroneous conscience judges wrongly through ignorance, a perplexed conscience cannot decide between two duties, and a scrupulous conscience sees sin where there is none.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Which alternative below best describes the effect of a poorly formed conscience?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The conscience is the inner guide used to judge right and wrong. If it has been badly formed, it guides the person towards wrong moral decisions. "Decisions" alone says nothing about the effect, and "weak" or "poor" decisions are vaguer than "wrong" decisions, which is the term used in the programme.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Which quality is best considered when choosing a friend?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Good character (honesty, respect, loyalty) is what makes a friendship lasting and healthy. Generosity, wealth and intelligence may be useful, but without good character they do not make a person a good friend.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Friendship becomes dangerous when
questions.corrige_markdown:
A friendship becomes dangerous when it moves from mutual respect to pressure for sexual intercourse, which can lead to pregnancy, disease and loss of self-respect. The other options describe poor habits or heavy demands, but the clearest danger is the request for sex.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love
O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

choix.texte: One makes many demands from the other.
One asks for sexual intercourse from the other.

questions.enonce_markdown: Mr Destiny travelled to London and her husband had sexual intercourse with their adopted child. What sin did he commit?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Incest is sexual intercourse between close relatives. Here the husband had intercourse with the family's own adopted child, who in the family is treated as his child, so the act is classed as incest. Adultery would involve a person married to someone else, rape needs a lack of consent, and abduction is taking a person away by force.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: When human beings have sexual intercourse with animals, it is referred to as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bestiality is the correct term for sexual relations between a human being and an animal. Fornication is sex between unmarried people, and "animal sex" and "occultic sex" are not technical terms.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: Self- stimulation for sexual excitement is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Masturbation is the stimulation of one's own sex organs for sexual excitement. Exhibitionism is showing the body in public, and "secret sex" and "self sex" are not accepted terms.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual relationship in which one party did not agree to is
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rape is sexual intercourse imposed on a person who has not consented. Incest is sex between close relatives and lust is a strong desire, neither of which refers to a lack of consent. "Forced sex" only describes the same act in plain words, while "rape" is the term used in the programme.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two people started a relationship that ended in marriage. Which is the love that has grown between them?

*Options as printed:* A) Agape.   B) Storge.   C) Erotic.   D) Philia.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Erotic love is the romantic, sexual attraction between a man and a woman that leads to marriage, so it is the love intended here. Agape is selfless divine love, philia is friendship and storge is family affection. Some textbooks may name storge for a love that grows slowly, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: C (Erotic).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love
O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: This type of love binds the family together.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Storge is the natural affection between parents and children and between brothers and sisters, so it is the love that holds the family together. Philia is friendship, erotic love is romantic and agape is selfless love for all.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love
O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the marriage of one man to more than one woman called?

*Options as printed:* A) Polygamy.   B) Polygyny.   C) Polyandry.   D) Bigamy.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Strictly, the marriage of one man to several women is polygyny. Polyandry is one woman with several men, bigamy is having exactly two spouses and polygamy is the general term for marriage to several spouses of either sex. Many local manuals give "polygamy", so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Polygyny).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: A mother who has never been married is called
questions.corrige_markdown:
A woman who has had a child without ever being married is a single mother. A single parent can be a father or a mother, a spinster is an unmarried woman without reference to children, and "lonely mother" is not a technical term.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Neba marries Manka, his late brother's wife. What type of marriage are they involved in?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Levirate marriage is the marriage of a man to the widow of his dead brother. Sororate is the opposite case, where a man marries his late wife's sister. Widow inheritance describes the practice more loosely, and nothing in the question suggests force.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family
O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these can be an obstacle to marriage?

*Options as printed:* A) Adoption.   B) Illness.   C) Infidelity.   D) Barrenness,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Obstacles (impediments) to marriage are conditions that prevent or hinder a marriage, and in many African traditions barrenness is often cited. Illness might also be argued, while adoption does not prevent marriage and infidelity is a fault committed inside a marriage. Because two options are defensible, the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Barrenness,).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Marriage between two people of the same sex is described as
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Gay marriage" (also called same-sex marriage) is the term used for the marriage of two people of the same sex. "Homosexual" is an adjective or noun for a person, not a type of marriage, "lesbian marriage" covers only two women and "mutual marriage" is not a term. This is a question of vocabulary only, not a judgement on the practice.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity
O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is responsible for the increase of single mothers in our society today?

*Options as printed:* A) Death of a spouse,   B) Pre-marital sex.   C) Divorce of spouse.   D) Infidelity of spouse.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the programme, the rise in single mothers is linked mainly to pre-marital sex, since many young women become pregnant before marriage. Death, divorce and infidelity of a spouse also leave one parent alone, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Pre-marital sex).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family
O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: How do we call a family of father, mother and their biological children?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A nuclear family is made up of a father, a mother and their children. The other names are not standard terms.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which ONE is an essential property of a home?

*Options as printed:* A) It provides education.   B) It provides food.   C) It brings up children.   D) It makes choices.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The home is the basic unit of society where children are born, cared for and brought up. Education and food are part of that task, so several options are partly right and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: C (It brings up children).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
Broken home implies that the couple

*Options as printed:* A) is divided.   B) has problems,   C) is working individually.   D) is separated.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A broken home is one in which the couple has separated or divorced, so the family no longer lives together. "Is divided" is close in meaning, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (is separated).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is common violation of human Life?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Abortion, the deliberate ending of a pregnancy, is the most common violation of human life named in the programme, because it takes the life of an unborn child. Organ transplant can save life, while sterilization and mutilation affect the body but do not end life.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: The act of deliberately ending the life of someone who is terminally ill is called
questions.corrige_markdown:
Euthanasia, or "mercy killing", is the deliberate ending of the life of a person with an incurable illness in order to end suffering. Manslaughter, murder and homicide are legal terms for killing in general.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the statements below is true about HIV/AIDS?
questions.corrige_markdown:
At present there is no cure for HIV/AIDS, only treatment that controls the virus, so "it cannot be cured" is true. It is not the greatest killer or the most recent disease, and it kills people of every age, not only young people.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - hiv and aids

choix.texte: It is the most recent disease.

questions.enonce_markdown: Criminal abortion is morally wrong because
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, life begins at conception, so criminal abortion is morally wrong because it takes the life of another human being. Risk to the mother, childlessness and prison are consequences, not the moral reason.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

choix.texte: It takes the life of another human being
The mother's life is at risk
The mother can go to prison

questions.enonce_markdown: The artificial process used in producing people who have the same features is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
Reproductive cloning produces a human being genetically identical to another. Therapeutic cloning produces cells or tissue for medical use, not a whole person, and insemination is the placing of sperm in the female body. "Cloning" alone is too general.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
Taking birth control pills is bad because

*Options as printed:* A) It is against God's law.   B) It is expensive.   C) It is dangerous.   D) It is an unhealthy idea.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the teaching of some Christian churches (for example the Catholic Church), artificial contraception is against God's law because it separates the sexual act from the possibility of life. Other traditions do not hold this view and pills are also discussed for cost and health reasons, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (It is against God's law).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
An example of a good family planning method of birth control is

*Options as printed:* A) Use of condoms.   B) Use of pills.   C) Use of the withdrawal method.   D) Use of natural herbs.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Churches that reject artificial contraception accept natural methods of family planning, based on observing the body, and "natural" is the only option close to that idea. No option is exact (periodic abstinence is the usual example), so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Use of natural herbs).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics
O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following drugs is the most intoxicating?

*Options as printed:* A) Alcohol.   B) Marijuana.   C) Kolanuts.   D) Cigarettes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Alcohol is the most widely used intoxicating drug and makes a person drunk. Kolanuts and cigarettes contain stimulants but are not strongly intoxicating, while marijuana is also intoxicating, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Alcohol).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these is a common cause of drug abuse?

*Options as printed:* A) Frustration.   B) Availability.   C) Idleness.   D) Lack of self-control.
questions.corrige_markdown:
People often turn to drugs to escape frustration and problems. Availability, idleness and lack of self-control are also commonly given as causes, so more than one option is defensible and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Frustration).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown:
The obligation to work comes from the fact that

*Options as printed:* A) We need the goods and services.   B) It is a command from God.   C) We exercise the body.   D) We earn a living.
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, work is a duty given by God to human beings (the command to work and to care for creation). Needing goods and earning a living are practical reasons, so the question is left open because the answer depends on the tradition taught.

**Intended answer: B (It is a command from God).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: Workers can better defend their rights by
questions.corrige_markdown:
Workers are stronger when united, so forming trade unions is the best way to defend their rights, and a union can then negotiate, dialogue or, as a last resort, strike. A strike on its own or cooperating with the employer does not give the same lasting protection.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment
O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which other name can be given to leisure?

*Options as printed:* A) Time to play.   B) Time to sleep.   C) Time for other things.   D) Time to relax.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Leisure is free time used for rest and recreation, so "time to relax" is the closest name. Time to play is only one use of it, and sleep is rest, not leisure. The wording is loose, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Time to relax).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: A strike is said to be lawful when
questions.corrige_markdown:
A strike is lawful when it is a last resort, that is, after negotiations with the employer have failed. Violence makes it unlawful, and "nobody goes to work" only describes a strike without saying whether it is lawful. Preserving property is a good condition, but it is not what makes the strike lawful.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment
O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: Any group constantly destabilizing peace in a country practices
questions.corrige_markdown:
Terrorism is the use of violence and fear by a group to disturb the peace of a country. Vandalism is the destruction of property, and extremism and fanaticism are attitudes of mind, not the constant disturbing of peace.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - peace and reconciliation

questions.enonce_markdown: A disposition to give each one what is his or her due is
questions.corrige_markdown:
Justice is the constant will to give to each person what he or she is due. Love and charity go beyond what is due, and peace is the result of justice.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is NOT a type of justice?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The recognised types of justice are legal, distributive, commutative and social justice. "Domestic justice" is not one of them.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: What type of peace exists where there is no war between countries?
questions.corrige_markdown:
International peace is peace between nations, shown by the absence of war between countries. Internal peace is within a person, domestic peace is within the family and social peace is within a society.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - peace and reconciliation

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is the most severe form of injustice against the State?

*Options as printed:* A) Tax evasion.   B) Fraud.   C) Robbery.   D) Money laundry.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax evasion deprives the State of the money needed for public services, and it is the form of injustice against the State usually stressed in the programme. Fraud, robbery and money laundering are also offences, so the ranking is a matter of opinion and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: A (Tax evasion).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights
O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these offences is NOT associated with juvenile delinquency?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Juvenile delinquency means offences committed by young people, such as forgery, smoking and drug abuse. Adultery is a fault of married persons, so it is not associated with juvenile delinquency.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - juvenile delinquency

questions.enonce_markdown: The preacher who once said "Do as I say and not as I do," can be described as a
questions.corrige_markdown:
A hypocrite is a person who teaches others to follow one rule while not following it himself. A pretender and a deceiver are close in meaning, but "hypocrite" is the exact word for saying one thing and doing another.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the pair that stands for an aspect of injustice.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Discrimination (treating people unfairly because of who they are) and favouritism (giving advantages to some without merit) are both aspects of injustice. In the other pairs, one item (jealousy, hatred, violence) is an emotion or an act, not a form of injustice.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown:
Business people who avoid the checking and assessment of their goods are guilty of

*Options as printed:* A) Goods evasion.   B) Control evasion.   C) Tax evasion.   D) Price evasion.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Avoiding the checking and assessment of goods by the authorities is best called control evasion, since goods are escaping official control. The terms printed are not standard, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Control evasion).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights
O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which ONE of these is an effect of climate change?

*Options as printed:* A) Release of green- house gasses into the atmosphere.   B) Release of carbon monoxide by vehicles.   C) Environmental pollution,   D) Acceleration of global warming.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Release of greenhouse gases and of carbon monoxide are causes of climate change, and pollution is a related problem. The effect that follows is the acceleration of global warming. Wording is loose and pollution is also arguable, so the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Acceleration of global warming).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are in charge of fighting corruption in Cameroon, What will you do to someone who is suspected of embezzling public funds?

*Options as printed:* A) Arrest him.   B) Investigate him.   C) Interrogate him.   D) Report him.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A person who is only suspected should first be investigated, so that facts are collected before any arrest or charge, which respects the presumption of innocence. Arresting, interrogating or reporting could follow, so the order is a matter of procedure and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (Investigate him).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: Bribery could be fought through
questions.corrige_markdown:
Education changes attitudes and teaches honesty, so it is the lasting way to fight bribery. Arrests and imprisonment only punish after the act, and tribalism is itself a cause of corruption.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: One name that best describes a diviner is
questions.corrige_markdown:
In African traditional religion a diviner is a spiritualist, a person who consults the spirit world on behalf of others. A witch and a wizard are believed to harm people, and a demon is an evil spirit.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

questions.enonce_markdown: Sects differ from denominational churches in that
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sects usually claim that they alone hold the truth and that outsiders are wrong, while denominational churches accept that other churches also teach the truth. Reading the scriptures and being found all over the world are not distinctive.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

choix.texte: They read and master the scriptures.
They claim monopoly of the truth.
They are found all over the world.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is common to Sects and Cults?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sects and cults are described in the programme as exploitative, because their leaders often take money and labour from members. They are not described as non-commercial, honest or simply dependent on God.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: Who is a Diviner?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A diviner is a person who claims to know the future (and hidden things) through spirits or signs. The word "claims" is important, since the ability cannot be proved, so options that state it as a fact are less accurate. Knowing the past is not the main sense.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion

choix.texte: One who can tell the future.
One who claims to know the future.
One who claims to know the past.

questions.enonce_markdown: All these are forms of magic EXCEPT
questions.corrige_markdown:
Charms, sorcery and divination are all described as forms of magic or occult practice in the programme. Sects are religious groups, not a form of magic.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - african traditional religion
O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults
